dedupe_keys.name: ixmon open source drdos attack detection system for large internet exchange points

description: IXmon is a system for detecting distributed reflective denial of service (DRDoS) attacks at large Internet exchange points and peering hubs, built for a study of in-the-wild attacks seen at one large IXP. The paper, revised in July 2020, explains that such attacks remain popular and largely unmitigated and quotes the 1.3 Tbps memcached attack and the 2.3 Tbps CLDAP attack. IXmon was deployed at Southern Crossroads (SoX), an IXP-like hub giving peering and upstream connectivity to more than 20 research and education networks in the south-eastern United States; in about 21 months it detected more than 900 DRDoS attacks against 31 victim ASes, most lasting only minutes, and the paper discusses IXP-level mitigation. Producer: Karthika Subramani, Roberto Perdisci and Maria Konte. Coverage: measurements from one IXP-like hub in the south-eastern United States. Access: the paper on arXiv; the abstract describes IXmon as open source but no repository link was read here, so the release is not independently verified. Licence and cost: free to read; licence not stated for the software; the describing arXiv preprint is under the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence. Caveats: a single IXP-like hub was studied, and deployment needs traffic sampling at an exchange fabric. Simulation uses: the detector and the observed attack patterns give inputs for resilience and cyber-threat scenarios at exchange points. Related record: the PCH IXP directory (data-pch-ixp-directory).
